findings: Main at v221: units+syntax28s, Chromium browser step575s, cross1 tests446s, cross2 tests740s; browser installation6/39/71s. Cross2 is the pre-deploy critical path, not Chromium.
Successful v220 release: main596s/cross1465s/cross2789s/deploy18s/live691s; recorded job runner sum2559s. This is not billed usage.
Full runtime per Firefox versus WebKit is not reliably separable from existing combined steps; no invented precision. Per-command timing instrumentation required for next baseline.

The 18 UI modules are already internally sequential after previous startup failures. Preserve this property. Local-versus-live executions are distinct safety proofs, not automatically removable duplicate tests.
Playwright1.56.1 (Chromium/pixel baselines) and1.64.1 (Firefox/WebKit) differ; alignment requires compatible screenshot/browser validation, not blind version replacement.
No dependency lock or actions/cache in primary workflow. Install overhead is smaller than current test runtime; caching alone cannot justify a large wall-time reduction.
Current SW gate compares merge parents, which can conflate base and PR changes; CI contract changes must preserve actual asset revision enforcement and validate PR/base semantics.
Current pull_request event lacks ready_for_review/converted_to_draft/synchronize stage plan; all drafts currently run the whole three-job regression.
Production503 was proven only in41080709085 attempt1; no generic timeout-as-infrastructure classification. One targeted unchanged retry succeeded.
notYetProven: No after measurements or claimed savings
No changed CI workflow or test selection yet
No full critical-case FAST/INTEGRATION/RELEASE mapping accepted yet
No isolated per-engine timing where combined script lacked instrumentation
